## Geometry and fitting of fixed-order population closures {#sec-fixed-closure-trainability}

The finite-order population model has its own optimization geometry. Absence
of suboptimal local minima, a nonsingular prediction differential, and
convergence of its initialized gradient flow are distinct conclusions. This
section proves the first two in stated population spaces and a scalar
mechanism that proves the third on specific invariant families. These results
concern the exact closure, without a finite-width or all-time closure-error
assertion.

### The fixed-order model and its physical metric {#sec-fixed-closure-model}

Take normalized directions $u_a=x_a/\sqrt d\in S^{d-1}$, labels
$y_a\in\mathbb R$, and positive weights $\mu_a$ of sum one, for
$a=1,\ldots,m$. Write $\phi=\tanh$. On separate fixed probability spaces
$\Omega_1,\Omega_2$, with expectations $\mathbb E_1,\mathbb E_2$, let the
bounded feature columns be $b_1\in\mathbb R^{K_1}$ and
$b_2\in\mathbb R^{K_2}$. The moving state is
$X=(w,c,M)\in L^2(\Omega_1;\mathbb R^d)\oplus L^2(\Omega_2)
\oplus\mathbb R^{K_2\times K_1}$. The physical squared norm is the sum
of the two squared $L^2$ norms and the squared Frobenius norm. Define

$$
\begin{aligned}
Z_a^{(1)}&=w\cdot u_a,&H_a^{(1)}&=\phi(Z_a^{(1)}),&
a_a&=\mathbb E_1[b_1H_a^{(1)}],\\
v_a&=Ma_a,&Z_a^{(2)}&=b_2^\top v_a,&H_a^{(2)}&=\phi(Z_a^{(2)}),\\
f_a&=\mathbb E_2[cH_a^{(2)}],&r_a&=f_a-y_a,&
d_a&=\mathbb E_2[b_2c\phi'(Z_a^{(2)})],\qquad
\mathcal L=\sum_a\mu_ar_a^2.
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-fixed-closure-forward}

Here $a_a,d_a$ are finite coefficient vectors, while $d$ is input dimension.
In layer notation, $w$ is the population first weight $W^{(1)}$,
$c=W^{(3)}$, and the second weight action is
$W^{(2)}v=b_2^\top M\mathbb E_1[b_1v]$. Its actual adjoint is
$W^{(2)*}v=b_1^\top M^\top\mathbb E_2[b_2v]$.
The coefficient metric is Frobenius in $M$, as in
[the autonomous closure equations](07-observable-closure.qmd#sec-docs-global-nonlinear-l12249); it is not an independently chosen metric
on all operators $W^{(2)}$.

Differentiating the finite contractions gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
\dot w&=-2\sum_a\mu_ar_a\phi'(w\cdot u_a)
                  (b_1^\top M^\top d_a)u_a,\\
\dot c&=-2\sum_a\mu_ar_aH_a^{(2)},\qquad
\dot M=-2\sum_a\mu_ar_a d_aa_a^\top,\\
\dot{\mathcal L}&=-\|\dot w\|_{L^2}^2-\|\dot c\|_{L^2}^2
                         -\|\dot M\|_F^2.
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-fixed-closure-flow}

For example, $Df_a[\delta M]=d_a^\top\delta M a_a$; differentiating
$a_a$ supplies the first line. Thus the factors of two belong to the
unhalved weighted square loss. The equivalent saved state consists of the
complete joint laws $\operatorname{Law}(b_1,g,w)$ and
$\operatorname{Law}(b_2,c)$, together with $M$; separate marginals lose
the needed correlations.

The dictionaries and initialization are those of
[the exact coefficient target](07-observable-closure.qmd#sec-docs-observable-p1-l28) and [the compatible hierarchy](08-autonomous-computation.qmd#sec-docs-global-nonlinear-l13161).
We recall their finite definitions to fix every coefficient used below.
Let $g_i,\zeta_i^0$ be independent standard Gaussians on $\Omega_1$,
and let $\widetilde g_i$ be independent standard Gaussians on
$\Omega_2$, for $i=1,\ldots,d$. Put

$$
\begin{gathered}
\nu=\mathbb E\phi(G)^2,\quad
\tau=\mathbb E\phi(\sqrt\nu G)^2,\quad\alpha=1-\tau,\\
h_i=\phi(g_i),\quad R_i=\sqrt\tau\zeta_i^0+\alpha h_i,
\quad k_i=\phi(R_i),\quad B_i=\phi(\sqrt\nu\widetilde g_i),\\
\beta=\mathbb E[h_ik_i],\quad s=\mathbb E k_i^2,\quad\gamma=1-s,
\quad\eta=1/4096,\\
\ell_h=\sqrt{\nu+\eta},\quad
\ell_k=\sqrt{s+\eta-\beta^2/(\nu+\eta)},\quad
\ell_2=\sqrt{\tau+\eta},\\
b_1=(h/\ell_h,\{k-\beta h/(\nu+\eta)\}/\ell_k),
\quad b_2=B/\ell_2,\\
D=(d_hI_d\ \ d_kI_d),\qquad
d_h=\frac{\alpha\nu}{\ell_h\ell_2},\quad
d_k=\frac{\alpha\beta\eta/(\nu+\eta)+\tau\gamma}{\ell_k\ell_2}.
\end{gathered}
$$ {#eq-fixed-closure-p1-marks}

Here $G$ denotes a scalar standard Gaussian only inside the fixed scalar
expectations. All denominators are positive: $\beta^2\le\nu s$ gives
$\ell_k^2\ge\eta+s\eta/(\nu+\eta)>0$. Also $\beta>0$, since
$h\mapsto\mathbb E\phi(\sqrt\tau G+\alpha h)$ is odd and strictly
increasing. The prescribed state is $(w,c,M)_0=(g,0,D)$. Both the
correlation in $R_i$ and the response contribution $\tau\gamma$ are
retained.

These order-one lists omit only the inactive constant coordinates. Under
simultaneous negation of the lower marks, $w,b_1$ are odd; under upper
negation, $c,b_2$ are odd. Then $H_a^{(1)},Z_a^{(2)},H_a^{(2)}$ are
odd, their gates are even, and the constant pairings
$\mathbb E_1H_a^{(1)}$ and $\mathbb E_2[c\phi'(Z_a^{(2)})]$ vanish.
Every velocity in @eq-fixed-closure-flow preserves this parity, and the
constant row and column have zero velocity. This is the exact invariant
sector of [the exact antithetic folding](07-observable-closure.qmd#sec-docs-observable-p1-l197), with arbitrary full
$M\in\mathbb R^{d\times2d}$.

For $d=2$ and full orders $p=1,2,3$, retain instead all total-degree-at-most-$p$
Chebyshev products in $(h_1,h_2,k_1,k_2)$ and $(B_1,B_2)$, including
constants. The initialized-word prefixes add no bounded feature at these
orders. For the resulting raw columns $\psi_\ell$, set

$$
L_\ell L_\ell^\top=\mathbb E_\ell[\psi_\ell\psi_\ell^\top]+\eta_pI,
\quad b_\ell=L_\ell^{-1}\psi_\ell,\quad
D=L_2^{-1}CL_1^{-\top},\qquad\eta_p=[1024(p+1)^2]^{-1}.
$$ {#eq-fixed-closure-polynomial-dictionary}

The complete construction and contraction formula for $C$ are
@eq-docs-global-nonlinear-l13279 and @eq-docs-global-nonlinear-l13303.
In particular their dimensions are $(5,3),(15,6),(35,10)$. Positive
density of the transformed Gaussian core on its open cube implies that
the raw polynomial Gram is positive definite: an almost-sure zero
polynomial vanishes on that cube by continuity, then identically by the
one-variable polynomial root property in each coordinate. Distinct leading
monomials give independence of the Chebyshev products. In the order-one
odd sector, the same argument applies to the nonconstant linear features.

All these normalized coefficient-to-field maps are contractions, since
$\mathbb E[b_\ell b_\ell^\top]
=I-\eta_pL_\ell^{-1}L_\ell^{-\top}\preceq I$.
The lower carriers are nonatomic. In the odd order-one sector $b_1$ has
positive density on an open neighborhood of zero, and $b_2$ on an open
cube about zero: the inverse map is
$g_i=\operatorname{arctanh}h_i$,
$\sqrt\tau\zeta_i^0=\operatorname{arctanh}k_i-\alpha h_i$,
followed by invertible linear normalization.

For completeness, the finite-time characteristic existence needed below
does not require a fitting hypothesis. With
$\mathcal B_\ell=\operatorname*{ess\,sup}|b_\ell|$ and
$Y=\sqrt{\mathcal L(0)}$, the locally Lipschitz vector field in
$L^\infty(w-g)\oplus L^\infty(c)\oplus\mathbb R^{K_2\times K_1}$
has, at the zero-readout initialization,

$$
\|c(t)\|_\infty\le2Yt,\qquad
\|M(t)-D\|_F\le2Y^2t^2,\qquad
\|\dot w(t)\|_\infty\le4Y^2t\mathcal B_1(\|D\|_{\rm op}+2Y^2t^2).
$$ {#eq-fixed-closure-finite-time-bounds}

Indeed energy bounds $\sum_a\mu_a|r_a|\le Y$, and contraction bounds
$|a_a|\le1$, $|d_a|\le\|c\|_2$ give these inequalities. Bounded
marks and bounded derivatives of $\tanh$ make the integral equation a
contraction on a sufficiently short continuous-path ball. The displayed
bounds keep every finite-time path in such a bounded state ball; bounded
velocities give a Cauchy endpoint at any putative finite maximal time,
where the same contraction continues it. This proves existence and
uniqueness through every finite time, consistently with
[closure well-posedness and restart](07-observable-closure.qmd#sec-docs-global-nonlinear-l12310).

### The initialized coefficient map retains each input coordinate {#sec-fixed-closure-initial-map}

::: {#lem-fixed-closure-initial-map}
For the order-one initialization in @eq-fixed-closure-p1-marks there is
one continuous, odd, strictly increasing function $F_0:[-1,1]\to\mathbb R$
such that, in every finite dimension,

$$
H_0^{(2)}(u)=\phi\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^d B_iF_0(u_i)\right),
\qquad Da_0(u)=\ell_2(F_0(u_1),\ldots,F_0(u_d))^\top.
$$ {#eq-fixed-closure-initial-map}

Thus this code is nonzero for every unit input, is injective, and takes
opposite values exactly on opposite inputs.
:::

[]{#proof-fixed-closure-initial-map}

::: {.proof}
Define the fixed coefficients $a_{\rm reg},b_{\rm reg}$ by

$$
(a_{\rm reg},b_{\rm reg})=(\alpha\nu,\alpha\beta+\tau\gamma)
 \begin{pmatrix}\nu+\eta&\beta\\\beta&s+\eta\end{pmatrix}^{-1},
\quad m_0(x)=\mathbb E_\zeta\phi(\zeta+\alpha x),\quad
j(g)=a_{\rm reg}\phi(g)+b_{\rm reg}m_0(\phi(g)),
$$ {#eq-fixed-closure-regression}

where $\zeta\sim\mathcal N(0,\tau)$ is independent. Multiplying the two ridge inverses in
@eq-fixed-closure-polynomial-dictionary and conditioning on $g_i$ gives

$$
F_0(t)=\frac1{\tau+\eta}\mathbb E[j(G)
 \phi(tG+\sqrt{1-t^2}V)],\qquad G,V\text{ independent }\mathcal N(0,1).
$$ {#eq-fixed-closure-scalar-map}

This also proves @eq-fixed-closure-initial-map, because the conditional
law of $g\cdot u$ given $g_i$ has mean $u_ig_i$ and variance $1-u_i^2$.
We prove strict monotonicity without assuming $a_{\rm reg}\ge0$.

The inequalities $\sinh|z|\ge|z|$ and Cauchy--Schwarz give, for a
centered Gaussian $V_\sigma$ of variance $\sigma^2$,

$$
\mathbb E\phi(V_\sigma)^2\ge
\mathbb E\frac{V_\sigma^2}{1+V_\sigma^2}
\ge\frac{\sigma^2}{1+3\sigma^2}.
$$ {#eq-fixed-closure-variance-lower}

For the second inequality pair $|V_\sigma|/\sqrt{1+V_\sigma^2}$
with $|V_\sigma|\sqrt{1+V_\sigma^2}$. Consequently
$\nu\ge1/4$, $\tau\ge1/7$, and $\alpha\le6/7$.
Write $J(x)=\mathbb E_\zeta\operatorname{sech}^2(\zeta+\alpha x)$,
$J_0=J(0)$ and $q_0=529/1024>1/2$. Then, for $|x|\le1$,

$$
q_0J_0\le J(x)\le J_0.
$$ {#eq-fixed-closure-gate-bound}

For the upper bound, represent $\operatorname{sech}^2$ by its centered
interval level sets. The Gaussian probability of $[-R-a,R-a]$ decreases
for $a\ge0$, since its derivative is the density at $R+a$ minus that
at $R-a$. Integrating over levels proves the bound. For the lower bound,
the addition identity gives

$$
\frac{\operatorname{sech}^2(z+a)+\operatorname{sech}^2(z-a)}2
=\operatorname{sech}^2z\operatorname{sech}^2a
 \frac{1+\tanh^2z\tanh^2a}{(1-\tanh^2z\tanh^2a)^2}
\ge\operatorname{sech}^2z\operatorname{sech}^2a.
$$ {#eq-fixed-closure-gate-addition}

Gaussian symmetry and $|\alpha x|\le6/7$ reduce this to
$\operatorname{sech}^2(6/7)\ge q_0$. Indeed
$(2n)!\ge2\,12^{n-1}$ for $n\ge1$, so
$\cosh z\le1+(z^2/2)/(1-z^2/12)\le32/23$ on $[0,6/7]$.

Gaussian integration by parts, with vanishing boundary terms because the
activation is bounded, gives
$\mathbb E[\zeta k\mid h]=\tau J(h)$. Conditional Cauchy--Schwarz
therefore yields $\operatorname{Var}(k\mid h)\ge\tau J(h)^2$.
Since $\beta=\mathbb E[h m_0(h)]$,

$$
s+\eta-\frac{\beta^2}{\nu+\eta}\ge\tau\gamma^2+\eta,
\qquad 0<\beta\le\alpha J_0\nu\le\alpha\nu,
\qquad
0<b_{\rm reg}=\frac{\alpha\beta\eta/(\nu+\eta)+\tau\gamma}
 {s+\eta-\beta^2/(\nu+\eta)}\le\frac1\gamma\le\frac1{q_0J_0}.
$$ {#eq-fixed-closure-regression-bound}

Here $\mathbb EJ(h)=\gamma$; the upper bound on the numerator uses
$\alpha\beta/(\nu+\eta)\le1\le1/\gamma$.
Set $R_\eta=\nu/(\nu+\eta)\ge1024/1025>q_0$. The first normal
equation for @eq-fixed-closure-regression now gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
a_{\rm reg}+\alpha b_{\rm reg}J(x)
&=\alpha R_\eta+b_{\rm reg}\left(\alpha J(x)-\frac\beta{\nu+\eta}\right)\\
&\ge\alpha R_\eta-b_{\rm reg}\alpha J_0(R_\eta-q_0)
\ge\alpha[1-R_\eta(q_0^{-1}-1)]
\ge34\alpha/529>0.
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-fixed-closure-combined-derivative}

Thus $j'(g)>0$. Differentiating @eq-fixed-closure-scalar-map on compact
subintervals of $(-1,1)$ and integrating by parts in $G,V$ gives

$$
F_0'(t)=\frac1{\tau+\eta}\mathbb E[j'(G)
 \phi'(tG+\sqrt{1-t^2}V)]>0.
$$ {#eq-fixed-closure-map-derivative}

Explicitly the derivative before integration by parts contains
$G-tV/\sqrt{1-t^2}$; the $G$ integration produces a term
$t\mathbb E[j(G)\phi''(tG+\sqrt{1-t^2}V)]$, which the $V$
integration cancels. Bounded derivatives and Gaussian first moments
justify these operations. Dominated convergence gives endpoint continuity;
strict interior increase implies strict increase on the closed interval.
Oddness follows by Gaussian symmetry. Coordinatewise injectivity and
oddness finish the proof.
:::

### The architectural floor and absence of suboptimal minima {#sec-fixed-closure-landscape}

Every represented predictor satisfies $f(-u)=-f(u)$ at every state.
Group observations modulo sign, choose a representative $u_g$, and write
$u_a=\epsilon_au_g$ with $\epsilon_a\in\{-1,1\}$. Define

$$
\pi_g=\sum_{a\in g}\mu_a,\qquad
\bar y_g=\pi_g^{-1}\sum_{a\in g}\mu_a\epsilon_ay_a,\qquad
\mathcal L_{\rm arch}=\sum_g\sum_{a\in g}
 \mu_a(\epsilon_ay_a-\bar y_g)^2.
$$ {#eq-fixed-closure-floor}

Expansion of the squares, whose cross terms vanish by the definition of
$\bar y_g$, proves the statewise identity

$$
\mathcal L=\mathcal L_{\rm arch}
 +\sum_g\pi_g\{f(u_g)-\bar y_g\}^2.
$$ {#eq-fixed-closure-floor-decomposition}

::: {#thm-fixed-closure-landscape}
Every local minimum in the physical product norm attains
$\mathcal L_{\rm arch}$, and this floor is attained, in either of the
following spaces:

1. Order one, $d\ge2$, with arbitrary odd $L^2$ fields $w,c$ and
   arbitrary $M\in\mathbb R^{d\times2d}$ in the canonical invariant sector.
2. Full canonical orders $p=2,3$ on the circle ($d=2$), with all
   constant and polynomial coordinates, arbitrary $L^2$ fields and full $M$.

There is no sample-count, input-linear-independence, bounded-displacement
or matrix-rank restriction. For inputs distinct modulo sign the floor is
zero. This is a population landscape statement, not convergence of an
initialized optimizer.
:::

[]{#proof-fixed-closure-landscape}

::: {.proof}
By @eq-fixed-closure-floor-decomposition it suffices to consider directions
distinct modulo sign and prove zero loss. We first establish two facts
shared by both spaces.

The functions $z\mapsto\tanh(z\cdot u_a)$ are independent. Choose
$e$ outside the finitely many hyperplanes perpendicular to $u_a$ and
$u_a\pm u_b$. The nonzero numbers $e\cdot u_a$ have distinct squares.
Writing $\tanh t=\sum_{j\ge0}(-1)^jA_jt^{2j+1}$, the identity
$\phi'=1-\phi^2$ gives $A_0=1$ and
$(2j+1)A_j=\sum_{k+\ell=j-1}A_kA_\ell>0$ for $j\ge1$. The first $m$ odd
coefficients of a relation restricted to $z=te$ form an invertible
Vandermonde system. The same proof shows independence of upper ridges
with nonzero coefficient vectors distinct modulo sign, on any upper law
with positive density on an open neighborhood of zero.

At a local minimum one necessarily has

$$
r_aM^\top d_a=0\qquad(a=1,\ldots,m).
$$ {#eq-fixed-closure-small-set-condition}

To prove this, fix $c,M$ and put
$Q_\omega(z)=\sum_a\mu_ar_a(b_1(\omega)^\top M^\top d_a)
\phi(z\cdot u_a)$. The loss is $C^2$ in the finitely many moments
$a_a$, with a uniform quadratic remainder near the current moments;
bounded marks, bounded gates, and $\mathbb E|c|\le\|c\|_2$ justify
this assertion. If $w(\omega)$ fails to minimize $Q_\omega$ over
finite $z$ on a positive-measure set, countability of rational trial
vectors and positive rational margins supplies a fixed $z$, $\delta>0$
and a positive-measure set where $|w|\le R$ and
$Q_\omega(z)-Q_\omega(w)\le-\delta$. Nonatomicity supplies subsets
$E$ of arbitrarily small measure $\varepsilon>0$. Replacing $w$ by
$z$ on $E$ changes its squared $L^2$ norm by $O(\varepsilon)$,
each $a_a$ by $O(\varepsilon)$, and the loss by at most
$-2\delta\varepsilon+O(\varepsilon^2)<0$. In the odd sector work
on $\{g_1>0\}$ and make the reflected change $-z$ on $-E$;
both the leading decrease and the moment changes are doubled and parity
is preserved. Such subsets exist because
$t\mapsto\mathbb P(E_0\cap\{g_1\le t\})$ is continuous for any
measurable $E_0$. Hence $w$ minimizes $Q_\omega$ almost surely.

Since $Q_\omega(0)=0$, this gives $Q_\omega(w)\le0$. Matrix
stationarity yields
$\mathbb E_1Q_\omega(w)=\frac12\langle\nabla_M\mathcal L,M\rangle_F=0$.
The odd function $Q_\omega$ therefore has minimum zero and is identically
zero. Ridge independence and positivity of the lower feature Gram prove
@eq-fixed-closure-small-set-condition.

Let $\mathcal H_2=\operatorname{span}\{H_a^{(2)}\}$ and let
$V_M=\{b_2^\top Mv:v\in\mathbb R^{K_1}\}$ be the current upper
preactivation space. Replacing $c$ by $c+\varepsilon k$ with
$k\perp\mathcal H_2$ preserves all predictions. A sufficiently nearby
equal-value state remains a local minimum in a smaller ball. Applying
@eq-fixed-closure-small-set-condition before and after the change shows
that any nonzero residual forces

$$
\phi'(Z_a^{(2)})V_M\subseteq\mathcal H_2.
$$ {#eq-fixed-closure-forced-inclusion}

Indeed subtract the two conditions and pair with any coefficient vector;
orthogonal decomposition in $L^2$ gives the inclusion. In the odd sector
all functions used here are odd, so the required orthogonal residual is
an allowed readout variation.

For the odd order-one sector, $M\ne0$ makes
@eq-fixed-closure-forced-inclusion impossible. More precisely, for any
$z\ne0$ and any $v,v_1,\ldots,v_m$,
$(b^\top z)\operatorname{sech}^2(b^\top v)$ is outside the span of
$\tanh(b^\top v_j)$. An alleged relation holds on the open upper cube
by continuity and density. On a line $b=te$ chosen with $e\cdot z\ne0$
and, if $v\ne0$, $e\cdot v\ne0$, it reads
$ct\operatorname{sech}^2(at)=\sum_jc_j\tanh(a_jt)$.
If $a=0$, real-analytic continuation makes the unbounded left side equal
to a bounded function on the real line. If $a\ne0$, the left side has
a double pole at $t=i\pi/(2a)$, whereas every right-hand term has at
most a simple pole there. This comparison is legitimate: multiplication
by $\cosh^2(at)\prod_j\cosh(a_jt)$ gives entire functions agreeing
on a real interval, hence everywhere by their Taylor series and analytic
continuation. Their unequal pole orders contradict the identity.
Taking $z=Mv\ne0$ proves that all residuals vanish when $M\ne0$.

If $M=0$, predictions vanish for every $w,c$. Write
$v_c=\mathbb E_2[b_2c]$ and
$A_y(w)=\sum_a\mu_ay_aa_a(w)$. Then
$\nabla_M\mathcal L=-2v_cA_y^\top$.
Unless every label is zero, the odd ridge function
$Q(z)=\sum_a\mu_ay_a\phi(z\cdot u_a)$ is nonzero.
Arbitrarily small odd readout changes make $v_c\ne0$, by adding a
linear feature and using the positive upper Gram. Arbitrarily small odd
lower changes make $A_y\ne0$: if it is zero, some component of
$b_1[Q(z)-Q(w)]$ has a fixed nonzero sign on a positive-measure bounded-$w$
set, for a rational $z$. Otherwise countability, continuity and
$b_1\ne0$ almost surely would make $Q$ constant, contrary to its
oddness and nonzero character. A small reflected-set replacement changes
that component by a nonzero amount. Both changes preserve zero prediction
at $M=0$. At the resulting nearby state, the direction
$\delta M=v_cA_y^\top$ has loss derivative
$-2|v_c|^2|A_y|^2<0$. This excludes a positive-loss local minimum at
$M=0$ and proves the first case.

For the full polynomial dictionaries, $V_M$ is a finite-dimensional
space of polynomials in $(B_1,B_2)$. If it contains a nonconstant
polynomial, @eq-fixed-closure-forced-inclusion is again impossible.
If $P=Z_a^{(2)}$ is nonconstant, use $P\in V_M$ itself. A proposed
identity $P\operatorname{sech}^2P=\sum_jc_j\tanh P_j$ holds on
the open cube. Restrict to a real affine line along which $P$ is
nonconstant. The restricted nonconstant polynomials have only finitely
many complex critical points. Among the infinitely many preimages of
$i\pi(n+1/2)$ under the nonconstant polynomial $P$, choose one outside
all those critical points. At it $P\operatorname{sech}^2P$ has a
double pole with nonzero coefficient and every $\tanh P_j$ has at most
a simple pole. Multiplication by the finitely many entire denominators,
as above, justifies meromorphic continuation and gives a contradiction.
If $P$ is constant, use any nonconstant element of $V_M$ on a line
where it is nonconstant: its product with the positive constant
$\operatorname{sech}^2P$ is unbounded on the real line, while the
finite tanh sum is bounded. Thus every residual vanishes unless
$V_M\subseteq\operatorname{span}\{1\}$.

In the remaining case write $b_2^\top M=v^\top$, so
$f_a=(\mathbb E_2c)\phi(v\cdot a_a)$. At a positive-loss local
minimum, @eq-fixed-closure-small-set-condition makes $\mathbb E_2c=0$
if $v\ne0$; if $v=0$ predictions already vanish. All lower-field
changes then preserve zero prediction. We show
$\mathbb E_2[b_2c]=0$. If this vector were nonzero, matrix stationarity
at all nearby lower fields would give

$$
\sum_a\mu_ar_a\phi'(v\cdot a_a)a_a=0.
$$ {#eq-fixed-closure-constant-image}

Replace $w$ by a bounded truncation still inside the local-minimum ball.
Along $w_t=(1-t)w_b+tz$ for any fixed finite $z$, the expression in
@eq-fixed-closure-constant-image is real analytic for all real $t$.
On compact $t$ intervals all tanh arguments are bounded, so a small
complex neighborhood avoids poles uniformly; bounded marks permit
integration of these holomorphic functions. The outer gates have the same
property. The identity near zero therefore extends to $t=1$.
With $a_0=\mathbb E_1b_1\ne0$ and $\kappa=v\cdot a_0$, this gives
$\sum_a\mu_ar_a h_\kappa(z\cdot u_a)=0$ for every $z$, where
$h_\kappa(t)=\phi(t)\phi'(\kappa\phi(t))$.
This bounded, odd, real-analytic function has derivative one at zero and
infinitely many nonzero odd Taylor coefficients: a finite series would
make it a bounded nonconstant polynomial on the real line. Choose any
$m$ nonzero coefficients and the same generic line used above. The
resulting generalized Vandermonde matrix at distinct positive squared
projections is invertible. To verify this, a polynomial with $m$ nonzero
monomials has at most $m-1$ positive roots: divide by the lowest monomial
and use induction and Rolle's theorem on its derivative. A singular
evaluation matrix would contradict this bound. Thus $r=0$, contradicting
positive loss, and proving $\mathbb E_2[b_2c]=0$.

If $v=0$, add a small constant to $c$; predictions stay zero but
$\mathbb E_2[b_2c]$ changes by a nonzero multiple of
$\mathbb E_2b_2\ne0$. If $v\ne0$, add
$\varepsilon(B-\mathbb E_2B)$ for any nonconstant upper mark combination
$B=e^\top b_2$. Its mean is zero, so predictions again stay zero, but
$e^\top\mathbb E_2[b_2(B-\mathbb E_2B)]=\operatorname{Var}(B)>0$.
Both contradict the necessary condition just proved. This completes the
local-minimum argument for all full orders stated.

Finally zero loss is attainable. In the odd sector choose a vector $z$
with distinct nonzero squared projections $z\cdot u_a$. Put
$e=\operatorname{sign}(g_1)$ and $A=\mathbb E_1[b_1e]$, choose a
coefficient vector $q$ selecting the first forward mark, and set
$w=ez$, $M=e_1q^\top$. Then $q^\top A>0$ and the upper features
are $\phi(t_ab_{2,1})$ with nonzero, distinct squared $t_a$.
Their Gram is positive definite by the ridge argument. Its inverse gives
a bounded odd readout fitting any labels. For a full dictionary use
$w\equiv z$, $a_0=\mathbb E_1b_1\ne0$, choose $e$ with
$b_2^\top e=B_1$, and take $M=ea_0^\top/|a_0|^2$; the same
argument applies. Applying these constructions to the signed-group
averages in @eq-fixed-closure-floor-decomposition attains the floor.
:::

A limited dynamical consequence is worth separating: no neighborhood of
a suboptimal equilibrium is contained in its point basin for exact GF.
Every such neighborhood contains a state of strictly smaller loss by
@thm-fixed-closure-landscape. Its nonincreasing loss prevents convergence
to that equilibrium, because the finite contractions make loss continuous
in the physical topology. This gives no basin-measure or stochastic-escape
statement and no initialized convergence theorem.

### Lower-layer trainability despite upper collapse {#sec-fixed-closure-lower-trainability}

::: {#lem-fixed-closure-lower-submersion}
For three pairwise nonparallel directions in $S^1$, use the order-one
odd sector with $w-g\in L^\infty$. The differential of
$w\mapsto(a_1,a_2,a_3)\in\mathbb R^{4\times3}$ is onto using bounded
odd perturbations.
:::

[]{#proof-fixed-closure-lower-submersion}

::: {.proof}
The adjoint kernel condition for coefficient vectors $\xi_a\in\mathbb R^4$
is

$$
\sum_{a=1}^3(b_1\cdot\xi_a)\phi'(w\cdot u_a)u_a=0
\quad\text{almost surely}.
$$ {#eq-fixed-closure-lower-kernel}

The unique dependence $\sum_a\lambda_au_a=0$ has all
$\lambda_a\ne0$. If one $\xi_a=0$, independence of the other two
directions and positive lower density force all three to vanish.
Otherwise @eq-fixed-closure-lower-kernel makes
$(b_1\cdot\xi_a)\phi'(w\cdot u_a)/\lambda_a$ equal for every $a$.
On a small ball about zero in the lower-mark support, the recovered $g$
is bounded. Bounded $w-g$ therefore bounds every gate between a common
positive constant and one. Thus
$|b_1\cdot\xi_a|\le C|b_1\cdot\xi_b|$ there, first almost surely
and then everywhere by positive density and continuity. Kernel inclusion
for nonzero linear forms makes all $\xi_a$ proportional. Cancel their
common linear form outside its null hyperplane. The gate ratios must then
be positive constants almost surely. Since

$$
\log\operatorname{sech}^2z
=-2|z|+\log4-2\log(1+e^{-2|z|}),
$$ {#eq-fixed-closure-log-gate}

this bounds $\big||w\cdot u_a|-|w\cdot u_b|\big|$, and hence the
same expression with $g$, almost surely. The latter is unbounded: near
$g=tu_a$ it grows as $t(1-|u_a\cdot u_b|)$, and neighborhoods of
arbitrarily large such points have positive Gaussian measure.
This contradiction proves injectivity of the adjoint $J^*$.
Consequently $JJ^*$ is positive definite and $J^*(JJ^*)^{-1}$ is a
right inverse. Its outputs are bounded because marks and gates are
bounded, and odd because the gates are even at an odd $w$.
:::

::: {#prp-fixed-closure-collapse-trainability}
For every such triple there is a bounded-displacement odd state fitting
$(1,1,-1)$ whose upper feature Gram has rank one but whose complete
prediction differential has rank three.
:::

[]{#proof-fixed-closure-collapse-trainability}

::: {.proof}
The preceding right inverse permits a bounded odd perturbation of $w=g$
for which $a_1,a_2,a_3$ are independent. To verify this last step directly,
if the initial $4\times3$ matrix has rank $r$, use singular-vector
coordinates and prescribe a differential equal to one in its missing
diagonal positions and zero in the existing nonzero block. A three-row
minor along the perturbation has determinant a nonzero constant times
$t^{3-r}+O(t^{4-r})$; hence it is nonzero for sufficiently small $t>0$.
Complete the columns to a basis $(a_1,a_2,a_3,a_4)$ and choose independent
$z,z_\perp\in\mathbb R^2$. Define

$$
Ma_1=Ma_2=z,\quad Ma_3=-z,\quad Ma_4=z_\perp,\qquad
H=\tanh(b_2^\top z),\quad c=H/\mathbb E_2H^2.
$$ {#eq-fixed-closure-collapsed-state}

Then $M$ has rank two and the predictions are $(1,1,-1)$, with upper
features $(H,H,-H)$. Their common backward vector $d$ is nonzero because

$$
z^\top d=\frac{\mathbb E_2[(b_2^\top z)\tanh(b_2^\top z)
                  \operatorname{sech}^2(b_2^\top z)]}{\mathbb E_2H^2}>0.
$$ {#eq-fixed-closure-collapse-backward}

The integrand is positive off a null hyperplane. A vector
$\xi\in\mathbb R^3$ annihilating the full prediction differential
must in particular annihilate all lower variations. Lower submersion
then gives $\xi_aM^\top d=0$ separately for each $a$. Since $M^\top$
is injective and $d\ne0$, this forces $\xi=0$.
More generally, the complete annihilator condition at any state in this
class is

$$
\sum_{a\in C}\epsilon_a\xi_a=0\text{ for each nonzero code class }C,
\qquad \xi_aM^\top d_a=0\text{ for every }a,
\qquad \sum_a\xi_a d_aa_a^\top=0,
$$ {#eq-fixed-closure-full-annihilator}

where $v_a=\epsilon_av_C$ in each nonzero sign class and zero codes
contribute no readout condition. These are precisely the readout, lower
and matrix block conditions: ridge independence proves the first,
@lem-fixed-closure-lower-submersion the second, and direct matrix pairing
the third. Positive data weights do not change rank.
:::

These are constructed states, without a claim of initialized reachability.
The lower differential is onto at each such finite state; no uniform
lower singular-value bound along an unbounded trajectory is implied.

### A scalar prediction that protects its own feature norm {#sec-fixed-closure-scalar-clock}

::: {#lem-fixed-closure-scalar-clock}
In the fixed-order model, let
$U(w,M)=\sum_a\theta_aH_a^{(2)}$, with fixed real coefficients satisfying
$\sum_a|\theta_a|\le1$, and let $F(X)=\mathbb E_2[cU]$.
Start from $(g,0,D)$ and assume only
$C_0=\mathbb E_2U(g,D)^2>0$. The full ascent equation
$X_s=\nabla F(X)$ has a solution for every finite $s\ge0$ and obeys

$$
F_s=K,\quad q_s=2F,\quad
K=\|\nabla F\|^2=C+\|\nabla_{(w,M)}F\|^2,\quad
C=\mathbb E_2U^2,\quad q=\mathbb E_2c^2,
\qquad C\ge C_0,\quad K\ge C_0.
$$ {#eq-fixed-closure-scalar-identities}

For any $A>0$ there is a unique $s_*\le A/C_0$ with $F(X(s_*))=A$.
If the actual loss gradient on an invariant initialized trajectory is
$-2b(A-F)\nabla F$, with fixed $b>0$, its physical clock
$\dot s=2b(A-F)$ tends to $s_*$, and

$$
(A-F(t))^2\le A^2e^{-4bC_0t},\qquad
\int_t^\infty\|\dot X(v)\|\,dv\le\frac{A-F(t)}{\sqrt{C_0}}.
$$ {#eq-fixed-closure-scalar-rate}

The full state converges to $X(s_*)$ in the physical norm, in
$L^\infty$ for $w-g,c$, and in Frobenius norm for $M$.
:::

[]{#proof-fixed-closure-scalar-clock}

::: {.proof}
The same bounded-gate contraction argument used above applies to the
ascent equation. With $\mathcal B=\mathcal B_1\mathcal B_2$ and $D_0=\|D\|_F$, its exact
gradients give

$$
\|c(s)\|_\infty\le s,\qquad
\|M(s)\|_F\le D_0+\mathcal B s^2/2,\qquad
\|w(s)-g\|_\infty\le \mathcal B D_0s^2/2+\mathcal B^2s^4/8.
$$ {#eq-fixed-closure-ascent-bounds}

Indeed $|a_a|\le\mathcal B_1$, $|d_a|\le\mathcal B_2s$ imply matrix speed at
most $\mathcal B s$ and lower speed at most $\mathcal B s(D_0+\mathcal B s^2/2)$.
These bounds and bounded velocities give continuation through every finite
$s$, before making any fitting argument.

Linearity in $c$ gives $c_s=U$, $q_s=2F$ and $F_s=K$.
At zero the hidden gradients vanish, so
$c(s)=sU_0+o(s)$, $F(s)=sC_0+o(s)$ and
$q(s)=s^2C_0+o(s^2)$. Thus $F,q>0$ for $s>0$, and
Cauchy--Schwarz gives $F^2\le qC\le qK$. Therefore

$$
\left(\frac q{F^2}\right)_s
=-\frac{2(qK-F^2)}{F^3}\le0,\qquad
\lim_{s\downarrow0}\frac q{F^2}=\frac1{C_0},\qquad
q\le F^2/C_0,\quad C\ge F^2/q\ge C_0.
$$ {#eq-fixed-closure-normalized-readout}

Integrate from a positive lower endpoint and then let it decrease to zero;
no continuous ambient extension of the ratio is assumed. The inequality
$F_s\ge C_0$ proves the unique crossing and its bound. On $[0,s_*]$,
$K$ is continuous and bounded. The residual $e=A-F$ under the physical
clock satisfies $\dot e=-2bKe$, hence
$e(t)=A\exp(-2b\int_0^tK(s(v))\,dv)>0$ at finite time. The clock
increases to $s_*$: any smaller limit would have positive speed. This
proves the exponential bound and identifies the physical solution by
uniqueness. Finally $\|\dot X\|=2be\sqrt K\le-\dot e/\sqrt{C_0}$,
which gives the length bound. Continuity at the finite ascent endpoint
gives convergence in the stronger characteristic norms. Coupling the
complete frozen marks identically also gives $\mathcal W_2$ convergence
of both saved joint laws.
:::

### Initialized training that reaches a positive architectural floor {#sec-fixed-closure-plateau}

::: {#thm-fixed-closure-plateau}
Use $d=3,p=1$, choose $0<a<1/2$, put $b=1-2a$, and take

$$
(x_1,y_1,\mu_1)=(\sqrt3e_1,1,a),\quad
(x_2,y_2,\mu_2)=(-\sqrt3e_1,1,a),\quad
(x_3,y_3,\mu_3)=(\sqrt3e_2,-1,b).
$$ {#eq-fixed-closure-plateau-data}

Define the initialized constants

$$
\ell=d_h\nu/\ell_h+d_k\beta\eta/\{(\nu+\eta)\ell_k\}>0,
\qquad k=\mathbb E_2\tanh^2(\ell b_2\cdot e_2)>0.
$$ {#eq-fixed-closure-plateau-initial}

Then the canonical full flow converges to a bounded state of loss $2a$,
with strict loss decrease at every finite time and

$$
\mathcal L(0)=1,\quad\dot{\mathcal L}(0)=-4b^2k,
\qquad0<\mathcal L(t)-2a\le be^{-4bkt}.
$$ {#eq-fixed-closure-plateau-rate}

Both hidden blocks have nonzero velocity for every $t>0$. There are
$\kappa_*\ge k$ and $C_*>0$ such that
$\mathcal L(t)=2a+bC_*^2e^{-4b\kappa_*t}(1+o(1))$, and the
characteristic state converges at rate $O(e^{-2b\kappa_*t})$.
:::

[]{#proof-fixed-closure-plateau}

::: {.proof}
Write $v=-e_2$ and $F=f(v)$. Oddness gives the exact ambient identity

$$
\mathcal L=2a+2af(e_1)^2+b(1-F)^2\ge2a.
$$ {#eq-fixed-closure-plateau-floor}

Reflect coordinate one of both Gaussian populations, using
$R=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1)$ and $R_1=\operatorname{diag}(R,R)$.
The measure-preserving maps $T_1,T_2$ satisfy
$b_1\circ T_1=R_1b_1$, $g\circ T_1=Rg$,
$b_2\circ T_2=Rb_2$, and $RDR_1=D$.
The physical isometry
$(w,c,M)\mapsto(Rw\circ T_1,c\circ T_2,RMR_1)$ fixes initialization
and sends $f(u)$ to $f(Ru)$. Since $Rv=v$, it preserves $F$ and its
ascent equation. Uniqueness makes the ascent path fixed by this isometry,
so $f(e_1)=f(-e_1)=0$. The full physical gradient along it is therefore
$2b(1-F)\nabla F$, without discarding a parameter block.

At $v=-e_2$, the two nonzero coordinate entries of $a_0(v)$ give
$Da_0(v)=\ell v$, with $\ell$ as displayed. Its positivity follows
from the positive constants in @eq-fixed-closure-p1-marks. The upper
coordinate is nondegenerate, hence $k>0$.
Apply @lem-fixed-closure-scalar-clock with $U=H^{(2)}(v)$ and target
one. It gives $s_*\le1/k$, $F(s_*)=1$, and
$\kappa(s)=\|\nabla F(X(s))\|^2\ge k$. The excess loss
$E=b(1-F)^2$ obeys $\dot E=-4b\kappa E$, proving
@eq-fixed-closure-plateau-rate, strict descent and attainment of the floor.

On the finite ascent interval bounded derivatives of $\tanh$ make
$\kappa$ locally Lipschitz and
$1-F(s)=\kappa_*(s_*-s)+O((s_*-s)^2)$, where
$\kappa_*=\kappa(s_*)\ge k$. Consequently

$$
\int_0^\infty|\kappa(s(t))-\kappa_*|\,dt
=\int_0^{s_*}\frac{|\kappa(s)-\kappa_*|}{2b(1-F(s))}\,ds<\infty.
$$ {#eq-fixed-closure-terminal-integral}

Near $s_*$ both numerator and denominator are of order $s_*-s$;
away from it the integrand is continuous. Thus
$C_*:=\exp[-2b\int_0^\infty(\kappa(s(t))-\kappa_*)\,dt]$
is finite and positive, and
$1-F(t)=C_*e^{-2b\kappa_*t}(1+o(1))$. Bounded ascent speed and the
linear endpoint relation give the state rate.

It remains to verify actual hidden motion. Reflecting each coordinate
orthogonal to $v$ as above makes $Ma(v)=\rho v$ throughout ascent.
Then $c_s=\tanh(\rho B)$, where $B=b_2\cdot v$, so $c$ depends
only on $B$. Independence and centering of the other upper coordinates
give $d(v)=\delta v$. Initially $\rho=\ell>0$. As long as
$\rho>0$, the integral
$c(s,B)=\int_0^s\tanh(\rho(\sigma)B)\,d\sigma$ has the sign of
$B$ for $s>0$, and hence
$\delta=\mathbb E_2[Bc\operatorname{sech}^2(\rho B)]>0$.
With $S=\mathbb E_1[b_1b_1^\top\operatorname{sech}^4(w\cdot v)]
\succeq0$, the exact equations give $a_s=SM^\top d$,
$M_s=da^\top$, and

$$
\rho_s=\delta\{\|a\|^2+v^\top MSM^\top v\}\ge0.
$$ {#eq-fixed-closure-plateau-hidden-motion}

A first-zero argument keeps $\rho\ge\ell$ forever. Thus $a\ne0$,
$\delta>0$ and $M_s\ne0$. Also $M^\top v\ne0$, and the positive
lower Gram makes $b_1^\top M^\top v$ nonzero in $L^2$. Multiplication
by the strictly positive lower gate shows $w_s\ne0$. The physical
clock is positive at every finite time, proving both motion statements.
:::

For $a=1/4$ the label masses are balanced, the limiting loss is $1/2$,
and $\mathcal L(t)-1/2\le\tfrac12e^{-2kt}$. The distinct inputs span
a plane. The positive limit is the architectural floor from incompatible
same-label antipodes; it is not failure to reach an available zero-loss
predictor.
